texts: On day 455 of Year 2, an apprentice named Eli arrived.
Eli came from a Keeper family.
The Council assigned Eli to Norren.
Norren had not taken an apprentice before.
Eli carried Norren's leather case from her second night.
Eli did not tend a lantern alone during her first six months.
Norren supervised Eli on every night of her first six months.

q1_issues.issue: `During` is used for the surface preposition "of" in "every night of her first six months" — the instruction set restricts `During` to during/while/throughout and names `During` for a surface "of"/"in" as the single most common head error.

"first" in "her first six months" is encoded as the property atom (Member sk_period_1 first) rather than the `Ordinal` head the instruction set defines for "the first N", inconsistent with (Ordinal sk_night_1 2 night) emitted for "her second night" in the same parse.
sk_period_1 never receives a kind atom — its only Member atom is the property `first` — so a referent symbol appears in the output untyped.

"Norren was a Council member" emits only the PartOf link; neither licensed route for a modifier+head NP is completed — no fused `council_member` typing with its genus, and no head-noun kind atom of the non-fusing part-whole route.

q2_gaps: A possessed, ordinal-modified time-span NP used as a discourse referent and temporal frame ("her first six months"): no rule says how to type such a span, how to rank it, or how to attach a stated extent to it (Measure … duration is defined for an eventuality).

"every night OF <span>" — a habitual whose recurrence is bounded by a span NP: the frequency machinery supplies the slot term plus (Every e 1 <cycle>) but has no carrier for the bounding period, which is why the parse reached for `During`.
An interval boundary anchored on an entity/period NP ("from her second night"): Start/End are specified with structured calendar terms, not witnesses.

A past-tense habitual ("supervised … on every night"): the frequency section says the event stays unmarked while the surface-tense rule requires (Past e) on a finite past clause; the parse emits both and the instruction set does not adjudicate.

A past perfect with the bare adverb "before" whose anterior anchor is an event in an EARLIER sentence: the ordering test is stated sentence-internally ("the sentence contains another asserted event") but its carve-out is stated text-wide ("no other event in the text"), and the bare sequence adverb itself has no licensed slot — it is dropped with no gap recorded.

A non-Gregorian calendar date ("day 455 of Year 2"): (Day n) is exemplified as day-of-month, so a day-of-year ordinal with no month has no stated convention (and the seeded date-ordering rules key on same-year-month day).
review.notes: Roles, negation scope (the alone-depictive and the indefinite lantern both stay inside the strength-0 bundle), tense wrapping of the PartOf, coreference of "her"/"the Council", and the leather_case / keeper_family decompositions are all handled correctly. The weak area is the two time-span NPs, where an unlicensed-slot approximation was chosen over recording the gap.

issues.reason: The Time section restricts During to "during / while / throughout" and names During for a surface "in" / "of" as the single most common head error; here the surface word is "of" and the second argument sk_period_1 is a span entity, not the reified eventuality During requires.

The half that stands is the intra-parse inconsistency — the same ordinal-modifier construction gets (Ordinal sk_night_1 2 night) for "her second night" but a bare property atom for "her first six months", and an atom emitted only sometimes makes two faithful parses differ; the half that is overstated is that Ordinal was cleanly available, since its <scale> slot is defined as the associated event or an explicit "-est" dimension and neither exists for a bare span (the reviewer's own first gap).

Names and casing states that a witness's class atom is always emitted and "an untyped referent symbol must never appear in the output"; sk_period_1's only Member atom is the property first, so its kind is never stated.

The part-whole route of Compound concepts requires emitting the head as its own kind AND attaching it with PartOf, and Categorical statements requires a Member atom for an individual subject of "X was a N" — the parse emits the PartOf alone, so Norren is never typed by the clause's own predicate nominal.

a non-Gregorian calendar date ("day 455 of Year 2"): (Day n) is exemplified only as day-of-month, so a monthless day-of-year ordinal has no stated convention
new_gaps: an ordinal on a bare counted noun with no associated event and no "-est" dimension ("her second night", "her first six months"): Ordinal's <scale> slot has no licensed filler — the parse substitutes the referent's own kind (night), which nothing licenses, and the reserved symbol unspecified is permitted only in Measure-family scale / unit slots
adjudication.defect_summary: For "on every night of her first six months" no compliant form is licensed for the bounding span — the frequency machinery has no slot for it — so the compliant parse keeps (Time e night) + (Every e 1 day) and leaves the span unencoded, since During is expressly barred for a surface "of"; sk_period_1 must carry its head noun's class atom, e.g. (GroupOf sk_period_1 month) with (Cardinality sk_period_1 6), so no referent symbol is untyped; and "Norren was a Council member" must emit the clause's own typing under the past wrapper — (Past (Member norren member)) beside the PartOf, or the fused (Past (Member norren council_member)) plus (Inheritance council_member member).
adjudication.notes: Negation scope is handled well — the depictive "alone" and the indefinite lantern both stay inside the strength-0 bundle while no referent typing is wrongly sealed — as are coreference of "her" to Eli, the Name-less "the Council", and the leather_case / keeper_family decompositions. Note that the During at statement 36 is licensed (the surface word there really is "during"); only the statement-43 one is the error.
